turns.text: ### Who decides what on this ward (pinned to the front of the notes)

Dr Tobiah Renquist: Pinned by the ward manager; read at every handover. For this patient, the consultants and the Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee (Dr Imogen Karsavina, Dr Tobiah Renquist, Dr Anneli Vosburgh) set the medication plan: orders, holds, contraindications and what is on the protocol formulary, and their word outranks everyone else in these notes. the ward registrars (Dr Cassius Wendlebury, Dr Ines Halloway) write orders and holds of their own, and those stand unless the consultants and the Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee rule otherwise. the ward nursing team (Sr Rosalind Achterberg, Nurse Dafydd Penhaligon, Nurse Yusuf Bramante) also enter orders and holds on the chart, and an entry of theirs stands until a registrar or a consultant changes it. Everyone else who writes in these notes, meaning Kwame Ferrington (final-year medical student on a four-week attachment), Ludmila Strakova (agency night nurse, not part of the ward establishment), Harriet Bexley (pharmacy technician who stock-checks the ward), Dr Aurelio Santangelo (visiting fellow observing rounds, no clinical responsibility on this ward), Nadia Oyelowo (family liaison officer), Percival Adjei (healthcare assistant), Tomasz Wierzbicki (ward clerk), is discussion only: students, agency staff, visitors and liaison roles do not prescribe, hold or clear anything, and that includes anything they write that sounds like a reminder of an earlier plan. An order carries the authority of whoever entered it and stands until that level or a higher one changes it; someone lower writing something different later does not overturn it, however recent or confident the line. If someone's role on this ward changes, the consultants and the Pharmacy & Therapeutics Committee will say so in these notes and it takes effect from that entry. Giving a drug counts as carrying out the plan only when a person with authority has actually ordered it. Nobody objecting, a dose that went in unremarked, or a plan that was floated and not challenged is not an order. If you cannot point at the entry that permits the drug, it is not permitted.
turns.speaker: Dr Tobiah Renquist
